# `hs-run skills` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run skills` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `target_disabled` | The named skill is stashed. The envelope carries its stash path and the disabled dependencies it needs loaded first, in order. | `harness/plugins/hs/skills/use/references/mechanisms.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `catalog_broken` | The skills tree could not be read at all. The envelope's warnings carry the underlying error; repair the install before routing anywhere. |
| `catalog_ready` | The skills tree is readable. The envelope carries how many are loaded and which are stashed; picking one is the next move. |
| `target_live` | The named skill is loaded. Invoke it directly; the off-skill proxy has nothing to add for a target that is already there. |
| `target_unknown` | No skill by that name in the catalog. Re-read the listing or check the spelling — the tree itself is fine. |
